reasoning: The evidence clearly indicates that NASA's crewed lunar landing missions are scheduled for 2027-2028 at the earliest. Artemis II (February 2026) is a lunar flyby only, not a landing. Artemis III was originally planned as the first landing but has been rescheduled to a test mission in late 2027. Artemis IV is now targeted as the first actual crewed lunar landing, planned for 2028. The 2025 missions mentioned (CLPS, Intuitive Machines, Astrobotic) are uncrewed cargo/payload deliveries. SpaceX's Starship has experienced multiple test failures in 2025, further delaying development. No crewed lunar landing missions are scheduled for 2025. The evidence provides no indication of any alternative crewed landing program that could succeed by end of 2025.
